articles.title: White House teleprompter operator ordered to pay $172K for placing prediction market bets on Trump’s speeches
articles.summary: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced the penalties for Gabriel Perez, who made the bets through Kalshi.
articles.body: A teleprompter operator for President Donald Trump who made online prediction trades based on information from upcoming speeches has been ordered to pay $172,000, a federal agency said Friday night. Gabriel Perez used “material, nonpublic information” he obtained through his job to place “trades” on a prediction market, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission said in a news release. Perez was ordered to pay the money he made in profits, $107,539.02, as well as a civil penalty of $65,000. He’s also banned from trading on prediction markets for three years, the CFTC said. Perez made the trades through Kalshi. The CFTC said Kalshi assisted in the matter. “A Kalshi surveillance investigation caught a White House staffer engaging in prohibited trading activity. Today this individual was subjected to penalties by the CFTC and by our exchange,” Bobby DeNault, Kalshi’s lead lawyer, said in a post on X. “It doesn’t matter who you are: violate our rules or federal law and you will face the consequences,” he added. The White House did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment Friday night. Perez could not be reached for comment. The CFTC called it a case of insider trading, adding that Perez traded “presidential mention market contracts, which are event contracts reflecting words or phrases the President may use during his speeches.” Perez was a technical assistant to the president who had served as a teleprompter operator for Trump since 2016. The CFTC cited what it called Perez’s “exemplary cooperation” in the case when announcing the fine and penalties Friday. Then-White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt in July called the online trades a breach of ethics, and “deeply unfortunate and frankly a disgrace.” Perez was placed on leave in July and Leavitt said at the time that “this individual will no longer be here.”

articles.title: Ex-White House teleprompter operator to pay $172,000 to settle CFTC probe
articles.summary: Gabriel Perez made over $100,000 on the Kalshi prediction market, per the CFTC.
articles.body:
A former longtime White House teleprompter operator will pay $172,000 to settle a regulator's allegations that he improperly wagered on the words President Donald Trump would utter during speeches, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) announced late Friday.

Gabriel Perez, who regulators claimed made more than $100,000 on Kalshi's so-called "mention markets," will return those winnings and pay a $65,000 penalty, the commission said in a press release.

Under the commission's order, a three-year trading ban is also imposed on Perez.

"The order finds that between December 2025 and February 2026, while working as a teleprompter operator for the White House, Perez traded presidential mention market contracts, which are event contracts reflecting words or phrases the President may use during his speeches," the CFTC said in the release. "In his position, Perez had access to presidential speeches prior to those speeches being delivered and Perez misappropriated that information--in breach of his duty of trust and confidence--to trade presidential mention market contracts, generating over $107,500 in profits."

The commission said the penalty Perez will pay represents a "significant discount" due to his "exemplary cooperation with the CFTC."

ABC News first reported last month that Perez, a technical assistant to the president who has been operating Trump's teleprompter since 2016, was accused of having made tens of thousands of dollars by placing bets on more than a dozen of Trump's speeches and was in talks with federal regulators to settle the allegations.

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt told reporters, following ABC News' report, that Perez had been put on unpaid administrative leave.

The White House said it has strict ethics guidelines that staffers are expected to follow. In March, the White House issued an internal memo warning staff against using nonpublic information to place bets on prediction markets, sources previously confirmed to ABC News.

In addition to February's State of the Union address , sources said CFTC investigators allegedly discovered that Perez placed bets on more than a dozen Trump speeches over a three-month period, including a December primetime address, a January speech at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, and Trump's remarks in March during a Medal of Honor ceremony.

According to sources familiar with the investigation, Perez sat for an interview with regulators in recent months and acknowledged some of the trades. At some point during the investigation, the sources said the CFTC alerted federal prosecutors in Manhattan, who declined to open a criminal investigation.

Kalshi has a policy against users trading based on information obtained as part of their jobs.

In June, the company updated its policies to require users to disclose their place of employment.

articles.title: Vance, Zeldin ask for EPA probe into East Palestine train derailment response
articles.summary: Two Trump administration officials are calling for an independent Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) investigation into the government’s response to the 2023 East Palestine, Ohio, train derailment — which caused toxic chemicals to spill into the town. In a joint Friday letter, Vice President JD Vance and EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin asked the EPA’s acting inspector…
articles.body:
Two Trump administration officials are calling for an independent Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) investigation into the government’s response to the 2023 East Palestine, Ohio, train derailment — which caused toxic chemicals to spill into the town.

In a joint Friday letter, Vice President JD Vance and EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin asked the EPA’s acting inspector general, Nicole Murley, to conduct a “comprehensive, independent” probe into the Biden administration’s handling of the incident.

The request follows this week’s release of a government watchdog group’s initial assessment of the derailment, which found that chemicals spilled during this event could have endangered thousands of Americans.

“For over three years, the people of East Palestine and surrounding communities have lived with the aftermath of the critical decisions of the Biden-Harris Administration and Norfolk Southern,” Vance and Zeldin wrote.

“The response to the derailment, subsequent controlled release and combustion of hazardous materials, environmental contamination, and prolonged concerns regarding air, soil, water, and public health warrant continued scrutiny and oversight to ensure appropriate accountability and inform future actions,” they continued.

Documents obtained by the Government Accountability Project found that the federal Interagency Modeling Atmospheric Assessment Center (IMAAC) projected a day after the train derailment that around 18,000 people may have been exposed to toxic substances at levels “that could possibly result in at least severe injury.”

IMAAC specifically reported that 17,972 of these people faced potential phosgene exposure and 312 may have been exposed to hydrogen chloride.

In the weeks following the incident, a chemical plume — caused by a controlled burn of the spilled chemicals — reached 16 states, researchers found.

Phosgene, which is used to make pesticides and plastic, can cause breathing problems, headaches, blurred vision and other symptoms, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Hydrogen chloride can be formed from the burning of plastics and creates hydrochloric acid when it makes contact with water, the CDC states. Both hydrogen chloride and hydrochloric acid are corrosive, cause respiratory issues and can burn eyes and skin.

Vance and Zeldin said in their Friday letter that identified shortcomings in the government response to this incident could result in changes to emergency-response procedures, environmental monitoring or coordination efforts between government agencies.

“The people of East Palestine deserve a government that is transparent and accountable to them,” Vance wrote in a Friday social media post announcing this request. “If the Biden administration withheld public health risks from the community, they must be held accountable.”
